- Prove the left side of the `Iff` from the definition of Dirichlet convolution. Since `ArithmeticFunction.zeta d = 1`, convolution with `zeta` becomes a divisor sum; if the library’s convolution formula uses `f (x / d)`, reindex via the involution `d ↦ x / d` on `Nat.divisors x`.

- Prove the right side using the trivial-character factorization
  \[
  L(s,\chi_{\mathrm{triv},N})
  =\zeta(s)\prod_{p\mid N}(1-p^{-s}).
  \]
  Combine the standard limit \((s-1)\zeta(s)\to1\) as \(s\to1\) punctured with continuity of the finite Euler product, whose value at \(1\) is
  \[
  \prod_{p\mid N}(1-p^{-1}).
  \]
  The `NeZero N` assumption is essential here to define the trivial character and its prime-factor correction properly.

Finally construct the `Iff` by proving each direction with the corresponding unconditional theorem, without using the implication hypothesis, and pair it with the Chebyshev identity.
